protections: P1: DataDump.add() must confine the requested dump path to the customer's documentroot on the filesystem (DataDump.php:86-93) - the guard present is lexical only.

P2: The root export consumer must re-establish that a queued destdir is a real directory inside the customer's documentroot before it creates, chowns or removes anything (ExportCron.php:64-74, ExportCron.php:215-216).

P3: Export sub-directories (.tmp/mysql/mail/web) must be created, chowned and removed without traversing symlinks planted in the customer-writable destination (ExportCron.php:98-101, ExportCron.php:192, ExportCron.php:213).

P4: Root-side directory creation and chown for customer-supplied subpaths (directory-options path, domain documentroot) must stay inside the customer root and must not traverse symlinks (FileDir.php:51-107 via Apache.php:1199, Nginx.php:596).
P5: Root-side chown of the stats directory built from the customer documentroot must not traverse a customer-planted symlink (Statistics.php:156-161).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: makeCorrectDir/makeSecurePath normalize the value and the documentroot is prepended, so the path is already forced under the customer's home directory.
makeSecurePath already collapses every run of dots to one dot, so '..' traversal is impossible and a lone '.' component is harmless.
a symlink check can simply resolve the full target path; nobody needs a data-dump folder that does not exist yet.
DataDump.add() validates the path (DataDump.php:86-93) and is the only producer of type-20 tasks (DataDump.php:133), so the root cron can trust the stored row.
the extra equality tests on line 69 already stop the cron from touching the customers root.
$customerdocroot is computed right before it is used and looks like the customer's documentroot, so it is the natural base for any containment check.
the destination is inside the customer's own documentroot, so everything below it already belongs to the customer and chowning it to them changes nothing.
the report is about the data-export feature; directory options use their own validation (Validate::REGEX_DIR) and the stored path is prefixed with the customer root again.
a customer cannot choose an absolute documentroot (Domains.php:399) and the relative value is appended to the customer's own documentroot, so it stays in their tree.
the sub-directory name is a fixed setting and the path is built from the customer's own documentroot, so the customer can only affect their own tree.

conflicts.what: A realpath/symlink-resolving containment check at DataDump.php:88-91 rejects destinations that do not exist yet, but tests/Backup/DataDumpTest.php:92-100 requires the non-existent '/my-dump' to be accepted and ExportCron.php:68-71 is designed to create the destination on first run.

Re-checking containment in ExportCron::handle() with realpath(destdir) fails for a first-run export because realpath() returns false for the destination the cron is meant to create (ExportCron.php:68-71); the check has to resolve the deepest existing ancestor instead.

fairness_risks: Requiring the dump destination to already exist contradicts the documented create-on-run behaviour (ExportCron.php:68-72) and the existing test tests/Backup/DataDumpTest.php:92-100, which uses a folder that does not exist.

A blanket 'no symlink anywhere under the documentroot' rule would refuse legitimate web layouts (customers commonly keep a symlink such as a release or 'current' directory inside their docroot); the rule must be 'resolves inside the docroot', not 'contains no symlink'.

FileDir::makeSecurePath already rewrites any run of dots (FileDir.php:166-174), so an added rule that rejects such names would refuse legitimate directory names such as 'backup..2024'; today such a name is silently stored under a different name.

Dumps are meant to live inside the public documentroot (DataDump.php:88) and only the documentroot itself is forbidden (DataDump.php:91); a rule that forbids serving the dump would contradict the feature's design.

T8, T9 and T10 are outside the DataDump advisory; a hidden test for them is only fair if the task report is worded at the class level ('symlink-safe containment of customer-controlled paths'), not as a DataDump-only report.

design.why: T1 is the described surface and anchors the solver. T4 is the far consumer where the protection never existed and the natural dismissal ('add() already validates and is the only producer') is wrong - the deepseek profile. T7 is the how-type nested/trailing-slash route that no validation of the requested path can close, because the customer owns the contents of the destination and can plant '.tmp' before the cron runs - the mimo profile. T10 is a second implementation of the same root chown over a customer-docroot path that needs no queued job and no export setting at all, so it survives a solver who only hardens the export feature. The four have four different reasons to dismiss and four different fix sites (DataDump.add(), ExportCron.handle(), ExportCron.createCustomerExport(), Statistics::makeChownWithNewStats), and all are reachable from public statics/APIs so behaviour can be tested. T2/T3/T5/T6/T8/T9 are recorded but either share a guard with the chosen traps (T2/T3 with T1, T5/T6 with T4, T8/T9 as one helper fix) or are too far to test fairly.
